long_biography.plain_text:
After studying economics at Sapienza University, d'Amico entered maritime transport in 1973 with a focus on petroleum-product carriers. A decade later he joined the board and subsequently became chief executive. He assumed the holding-company presidency in 2002, guiding a period that brought new overseas offices, a stock-market flotation and extensive investment in more efficient vessels.

D'Amico has also headed Italy's shipowners' confederation, the global association for independent tanker operators and the Italian Naval Registry. He holds a major family ownership position in the private parent, which controls the quoted tanker arm. He directs the parent as executive chairman and presides over the listed tanker business.
